claim: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a serverless, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service for container metrics that makes it easier to securely monitor container environments at scale.
q: What is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/what-is-Amazon-Managed-Service-Prometheus
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a serverless, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service for container metrics that makes it easier to securely monitor container environments at scale.

claim: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus works with container clusters that run on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service and self-managed Kubernetes environments.
q: Which container clusters can Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus monitor?
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/what-is-Amazon-Managed-Service-Prometheus
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus works with container clusters that run on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service and self-managed Kubernetes environments.

claim: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus automatically scales the ingestion, storage and querying of operational metrics as workloads scale up and down.
q: Do you manage capacity for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?
v: automatically scales the ingestion, storage, and querying
as workloads scale up and down
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/what-is-Amazon-Managed-Service-Prometheus
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus automatically scales the ingestion, storage, and querying of operational metrics as workloads scale up and down.

claim: With Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus you use the same open-source Prometheus data model and PromQL query language that you use with Prometheus, and engineering teams can use PromQL to filter, aggregate and alarm on metrics without code changes.
q: Which query language does Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus use?
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/what-is-Amazon-Managed-Service-Prometheus

With Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, you use the same open-source Prometheus data model and PromQL query language that you use with Prometheus. Engineering teams can use PromQL to filter, aggregate, and alarm on metrics and quickly gain performance visibility without any code changes.

claim: There are two ways to ingest metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace: an AWS managed collector, a fully managed agentless scraper for Amazon EKS clusters, or a customer managed collector such as your own Prometheus in agent mode or the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry.
q: How do metrics get into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace?
v: installing your own instance of Prometheus
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-methods
There are two methods of ingesting metrics into your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-methods

**Using an AWS managed collector** – Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus provides a fully-managed, agentless scraper to automatically *scrape* metrics from your Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-methods
Two of the most common collectors to use are installing your own instance of Prometheus, running in agent mode, or using AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry.

claim: Metrics must be ingested into your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace before you can query or alert on them.
q: Can you query or alert on metrics that were not ingested into a workspace?
v: query or alert on those metrics
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-methods
Metrics must be ingested into your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace before you can query or alert on those metrics.

claim: The AWS managed collector is a fully managed, agentless scraper that automatically discovers and pulls Prometheus-compatible metrics; you do not have to manage, install, patch or maintain agents or scrapers, and it works with Amazon EKS clusters including EC2 and Fargate.
q: Do you have to run agents for the AWS managed collector of Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?
v: don't have to manage, install, patch, or maintain agents
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-collector

Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus provides a fully managed, agent less scraper, or *collector*, that automatically discovers and pulls Prometheus-compatible metrics. You don't have to manage, install, patch, or maintain agents or scrapers.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-collector
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus managed collectors work with Amazon EKS clusters, including EC2 and Fargate.

claim: A managed collector creates an Elastic Network Interface per subnet specified when creating the scraper, scrapes metrics through these ENIs, and uses remote_write to push the data to the workspace through a VPC endpoint, so the scraped data never travels on the public internet.
q: Does data from the managed collector travel over the public internet?
v: never travels on the public internet
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-collector

An Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector creates an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) per subnet specified when creating the scraper. The collector scrapes the metrics through these ENIs, and uses `remote_write` to push the data to your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace using a VPC endpoint. The scraped data never travels on the public internet.

claim: If you have multiple containers or instances that have the same data, you can send that data to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and have the data automatically de-duplicated.
q: How does Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus handle duplicate data from redundant collectors?
v: containers or instances that have the same data
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-high-availability
If you have multiple containers or instances that have the same data, you can send that data to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and have the data automatically de-duplicated.

claim: To keep access to your metrics even when the AWS Region is not available, you can send your metrics to a second workspace in another Region.
q: How can you keep Prometheus metrics available if a Region is down?
v: a second workspace, in another Region
even when the AWS Region is not available
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-high-availability
If you want to ensure that you have access to your data, even when the AWS Region is not available, you can send your metrics to a second workspace, in another Region.

claim: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports recording rules, which precompute frequently needed or expensive expressions and save the result as a new set of time series, and alerting rules, which define alert conditions based on PromQL and a threshold and send a notification to alert manager.
q: What two kinds of rules does Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus support?
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-Ruler
*Recording rules* allow you to precompute frequently needed or computationally expensive expressions and save their results as a new set of time series.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-Ruler
*Alerting rules* allow you to define alert conditions based on PromQL and a threshold.

claim: Alert manager in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports only Amazon SNS as a receiver and can route messages to SNS topics in the same account.
q: Which notification targets can the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus alert manager use?
v: only Amazon Simple Notification Service as a receiver
SNS topics in the same account
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-alert-manager
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports only Amazon Simple Notification Service as a receiver, and can route messages to Amazon SNS topics in the same account.

claim: When alerting rules fire, alert manager de-duplicates, groups and routes the alerts to downstream receivers, and you can also use it to silence and inhibit alerts.
q: What does the alert manager of Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus do with firing alerts?
v: de-duplicates, groups, and routes the alerts
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-alert-manager
It de-duplicates, groups, and routes the alerts to downstream receivers.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-alert-manager
You can also use alert manager to silence and inhibit alerts.

claim: By default Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus automatically provides encryption at rest using AWS owned encryption keys, and you can choose a symmetric customer managed key when you create your workspace.
q: Is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus data encrypted at rest and can you use your own KMS key?
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/encryption-at-rest-Amazon-Service-Prometheus
By default, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus automatically provides you with encryption at rest and does this using AWS owned encryption keys.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/encryption-at-rest-Amazon-Service-Prometheus
You can alternatively choose to use a customer managed key when you create your workspace:
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/encryption-at-rest-Amazon-Service-Prometheus
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports the use of a symmetric customer managed key that you create, own, and manage to encrypt the data in your workspace.

claim: You can query Prometheus metrics with direct queries that use the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus API and PromQL, or build dashboards with a service such as Amazon Managed Grafana, which can add a workspace as a data source.
q: How do you query and visualize metrics stored in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?
v: the standard Prometheus query language, PromQL
ev: docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-query
Direct queries use the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus API and the standard Prometheus query language, PromQL, to get data from your Prometheus workspace.
docs/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-amg
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports using Amazon Managed Grafana to query metrics in a workspace.
